en: One Fascicle of the Ritual Manual for Recitation of the Supreme Standing Mudrā of the Holy Unmoving Wrathful King of Great Majesty, from the *Vajrapāṇi-prabhābhiṣeka-sūtra*.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Da Xingshan Monastery—Great Preceptor of the Court, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Sushan with a fief of three thousand households, recipient of the purple robe, posthumously honored as Minister of Works, and titled Dajian (Great Mirror), bearing the epithet Dayangzhi (Great and Vast Wisdom)—by Imperial Decree. At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi entered the *samādhi*.
It is named the Vajra-like Samādhi of Blazing Radiance;
its light universally illumines all buddha-fields and completely incinerates the three realms.
All the māras therein who create obstacles and hindrances,
as well as all the vināyakas, rākṣasas, and so forth,
are all incinerated by this great fire.
Aching and piercing pain pervaded his limbs;
agonizing distress constricted and bound his body,
leaving his mind bewildered and fainting.
They all raised their voices and cried out loudly,
like worldly people who, when oppressed by great suffering, cry out "Mi-mi.
Their voices filled the entire trichiliocosm.
All sentient beings who heard this sound were filled with terror and fled;
they threw themselves before the Buddha and all spoke these words:
“World-Honored One, we now together take refuge in the Triple Gem.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi arose from samādhi and addressed Mañjuśrī, saying:
"How do you perceive the various Śakras, lords of the gods, coming here?
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva said to Vajrapāṇi, "I cannot know this; only a Tathāgata knows it."
Having spoken these words, the two great beings remained silent.
Then Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva again addressed Mañjuśrī, saying:
"There is a Great Wrathful King named the Noble Acala."
"I have now spoken of this mind and established the mudrās;
therefore, the entire great assembly has come here.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva again addressed Mañjuśrī, saying:
"Good son, listen attentively! The Tathāgata Boundless Power and Valiant Strength has served this Great Majestic Wrathful King Acala.
Furthermore, sixty million *koṭis* of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, have all received his instruction and attained unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
Furthermore, there are immeasurable devas, nāgas,
and the eight classes of beings who constantly make offerings, pay respect, and serve him.
If one merely brings this King of Wrathful Power to mind, [they will do so].
It can cause all those who create obstacles and difficulties to be completely severed and destroyed;
no obstructing beings dare to approach.
One should always remain far removed from such places where practitioners reside,
for there shall be no demonic activities nor any malevolent spirits and ghosts.
Then, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi arose from samādhi and,
having awakened them, summoned all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas,
as well as all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and all classes of living beings.
They all gathered together.
Furthermore, he extracted and synthesized the diverse minds of those various classes of sentient beings,
unifying them into a single essence and abiding equally in samādhi.
Known as the Great Majestic Power that Incinerates Worlds by the Koṭi,
it becomes a single great mass of fire,
like the radiance of seven suns.
The great rivers, such as the Mahānadī, all converge together;
he swallows them without exception until they are entirely transformed into fierce flames.
He then utters this subtle heart-mantra of the Great Fierce Wrathful King, the Noble Acala.
It is also like a great horse that swallows and devours the various minds of all sentient beings, equally forming a realm of great blazing fire.
*Namo sarvatathāgatebhyo viśuddhebhyaḥ sarvamukhebhyo viśuddhaḥ svāhā. Traṭ caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa kha khe khāhi khāhi sarvavijñānān hūṃ traṭ haṃ maḥ.* As soon as this sublime mantra was spoken...
The moment all the bodies were severed as if by a brandished sword,
they fell to the ground all at once, like a grove of plantains cut down by a sharp blade,
or like the leaves of many trees scattered by a great, violent, and fierce whirlwind.
He blew and cast the great assembly into the space between the Cakravāḍa mountains,
with the exception of the great bodhisattvas of the tenth stage;
thus it was for all buddha-fields throughout the trichiliocosm.
All were incinerated by the majestic radiance of the Great Wrathful King;
becoming a single mass of fire,
they formed Mount Sumeru and Mahāsumeru.
The Cakravāḍa Mountains and the Great Cakravāḍa Mountains,
as well as all the great oceans, will completely dry up and wither away,
being consumed by fire until they are reduced to ashes.
The great assembly all beheld it.
When one wishes to perform various ritual activities, first bind the *samaya* mudrā:
join the two palms together with the fingers extended like wheels, and raise both thumbs upright.
By virtue of this empowerment, the body becomes identical to that of the Tathāgata.
The Samaya-mantra is as follows: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām, oṃ samite samaye svāhā*. Next, bind the Dharmadhātu-mudrā.
With two vajra fists, the two wind fingers [of the hands] are pressed against each other on the sides.
The mantra is as follows:
Interlace the two palms with the backs facing each other; join the two space peaks together.
Adding five places to the body, the mantra for the Body identical to Vajradhara is:
*Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ vajratmakrodha*. Next, bind the secret mudrā of the Great Vīrya-Wisdom Sword.
With both hands in the *tripuṭa* [mudrā], bend the first joints of the fingers so that the tips meet and rest against the sky;
by binding this seal, all fetters (*saṃyojana*) are severed and destroyed. The mantra is as follows:
The sword mudrā is modified with the two empty [fingers] positioned between wind and fire;
this is called the Dharma-conch mudrā. The mantra is as follows:
Next, the offering of the flower-seat is called the Vajra-lotus.
The lotus of concentration and wisdom are joined; water and fire both disperse and open like the petals of a lotus flower.
The two winds bend and attach themselves, abiding beside the first joint of the fire. Thus one serves all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
The mantra is as follows:
Forming the wrathful bind with both hands, bend the two wind-fingers like hooks;
this is called the Secret Hook Seal (Ākarṣaṇamudrā), which is capable of accomplishing the rite of summoning.
The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām āḥ sarvatathāgatapratihata-tathāgatagarbha-maudgalyāya-paripūraka svāhā*. Next, offer the argha water.
First, perform the Śaṅkha-mudrā; then recite this secret mantra.

For the mudrā of offering scented unguent: join the two hands like lotus petals, with the vāyu-fingers (ring fingers) each flicked like a snap of the fingers, and the space-fingers (thumbs) joined together pressing against the vāyu-wheels (ring fingers).
The mantra is as follows:
Using the previously described ointment mudrā, place both thumbs at the lower joint of the ring fingers; this is called the flower offering mudrā.
The mantra is as follows:
With both hands, perform the *tripuṭa* mudrā. The earth fingers stand upright; the two water fingers rest beneath them;
the two fire fingers are bent at their upper joints; and the two little fingers are joined together below.
The two winds bend the middle joints; the peak rests upon the head of the void.
The mantra for offering incense is as follows: it also includes the *namas* (homage).
The mudrā for offering food and drink is: join the two hands with palms hollowed.
The mantra for entering the palms with meditative concentration and wisdom is: *Namo*.
Using the previously mentioned food-offering mudrā, change only this:
join the two empty wheels (the thumbs) and raise them apart like a full moon; this is called the lamp-offering.
The mantra is: *Namo*. Next, form the fundamental secret mudrā of Acala:
cross the two palms inwardly, with each wheel [of the thumbs] like a ring.
The two empty fingers [index and middle] rest at the side of the water; the fire-peak [ring finger] rests against the face of the sky.
The two empties are joined vertically. Next, for the seal of the Jewel Mountain, the wisdom and means [thumbs and little fingers] are crossed within, and the two empties enter into the full moon.
With two vajra fists, place the wisdom fist firmly upon the concentration fist;
this is called the Head Secret Seal. Placing the seal upon the head, interlace the two hands within, with the two thumbs entering to form a full moon.

The wind-mandala is joined vertically; sealing the eyes and the space between the eyebrows is called the Eye Secret Seal (*cakṣur-rahasya-mudrā*). Next, bind the Oral Secret Seal (*vāk-rahasya-mudrā*):
interlace the thumbs within and press the water-finger over the interlaced thumbs.
Extend both hands straight; place *a* on each space and *ka* on the two winds.
Placing the mudrā at the mouth, next is the form of the secret mudrā:
the two palms joined three times (*tripuṭa*).
Wind and space are like a finger-snap; this is called the Heart Secret Seal (*cittamudrā*).
Furthermore, there are three *puṭa*s: two fires are established like banners, with wind abiding at the first joint of fire; two waters are like the shape of jewels.
The two stages and the two voids are each established;
one seals the heart and both shoulders. Then, placing [the hands] at the throat and atop the head, one performs the *akṣapā* [mudrā], which is called the "Lion’s Agility" (*siṃhavijṛmbhita*).
Without altering the previous secret mudrā, extend the wisdom-wind wheel upward;
next, bind the flame mudrā by placing the space-wheel of the wisdom hand upon the water and fire armors,
with the wind wheel held upright, supporting the palm of concentration.
Turning to the right forms the boundary; turning to the left is called "dispersal.

For the mudrā that stops the wheel of flames: form fists with the hands of concentration and wisdom respectively, extending the index fingers between the fire and wind fingers; join the backs of the two fists together.
One is able to suppress all fires; next, with the *śaṅkha* secret mudrā, one stabilizes space and adds earth and water.
The wisdom-wing is likewise [arranged] as two fires, and the armor is like a needle.
One visualizes the wind-element attached to the fire-element at its joints.
Stabilize the wind-finger and extend it upright; with the immovable thirst-finger, seal the stabilization.
Add earth and water to the space-finger, and extend both wind and fire straight;
this is called the sheath of samādhi. The wisdom-hand is likewise.
Contemplate the wheels of wind, fire, space, water, and earth;
when their faces merge with the moon, the sword remains fixed in its sheath.
When drawn forth, it accomplishes all tasks, such as severing fetters, performing protections, and so forth.
Next, bind the noose mudrā: place the wisdom hand in the space gesture and add the water, fire, and earth wheels.
In the wind wheel, establish the *samādhi-moon* and rest upon the fists of earth, water, and fire.
Support the space and wind [fingers] like a ring.
This is called the lasso insignia; visualize the three-pronged vajra seal,
add the wind armor in space, and with all ritual implements like vajras in the three wheels, sprinkle and purify them.
The secret mudrās have been fully explained. The Noble Lord Acala teaches all mantras:

one should employ the aforementioned Vajra-mudrā while reciting this mantra: *Namo samantavajrāṇām | Hūṃ vikṛta-vikara-lodrava-keśa hūṃ vajragra gra hūṃ phaṭ.* This single mantra employs the Vajra-mudrā.
It is capable of accomplishing all undertakings.
Furthermore, the mantra is as follows: Using the *kṣepaṇī-mudrā*, recite:

*Namaḥ samantavajrāṇām | oṃ acalakañjam buddhāntaka hūṃ hūṃ kha hi kha hi īṃ gṛhṇa ratna maṃ hala hala viśvasapta a hrīṃ ju ho ha phaṭ ṭa āryācala-jeṣa-kintirāja tu īṃ kalaya kuru svāhā*. With this mantra, employ the aforementioned sword-mudrā (*khaḍga-mudrā*).
All undertakings can be accomplished. Next, for the one true mantra, employ the previous noose mudrā.
By employing the noose mudrā with the mantra, all matters can be accomplished.
Furthermore, for the heart mantra, employ the Vajra Secret Mudrā.
This mantra, when employed with the vajra-mudrā, is able to accomplish all activities.
Next, the practice of Amoghasiddhi is explained: whenever the noble practitioner of Acala has finished eating, he should empower [the food] with this mantra.
Place the remnants in a pure location and offer them to the Immovable One (Acala).
Next, regarding the Noble Immovable One, the Great Majestic Wrathful King:
by using this one-syllable heart-mantra, one can accomplish all feats.
To accomplish all activities, one universally employs all mudrās.
Furthermore, regarding the secret method of arranging the syllables of the Noble Acala,
one should place them one by one from the crown of the head down to the feet.
Placing the long *khaṃ* upon the crown, one accomplishes the *uṣṇīṣa*;
placing *ṅi* upon the head, one achieves the *śikhā-jaṭā*.
Placing *ki* on the left side of the head, one completes the hanging single-strand hair-tie.
The syllable *Aṃ* is placed upon the forehead, forming the mark of *ra-ra-ṭa*;
*La-hi* is placed upon both ears, accomplishing the adamantine ear;
*Tra* is placed upon the left eye, its character bearing a long vowel.
Place *Ṭha* in the left eye; the syllable *Haṃ* should not be fully elongated.
Place *Hūṃ* on both nostrils. Reciting the *Bhu*, this is the mantra;
the ninth rotation is the syllable *Ha*. It is named "Protection" and is placed in the mouth.
Recite *Ha* with a short vowel and a nasal dot (*anusvāra*)—this is named *Haṃbu*;
it forms the adamantine tongue-mark at the tip of the tongue. Recite this tongue-mantra.
Recite *Laṃbu* for both shoulders—this is the shoulder-mantra.
The short *maṃ* with a bindu is called *māṃ*, placed at the throat;
the short *ta* with a bindu is called *tāṃ*, placed on both breasts;
the short *ma* with a bindu is called *māṃ*, placed at the heart.
The short *ṭha* together with the nasal bindu is placed within the navel wheel;
because it is adorned by the great void (*mahāśūnya*),
it accomplishes the ninth transformation of the syllable *ṭhaṃ*, bearing the great void-bindu upon its crown.
Arrange [the syllables] on both flanks; recite this flank-mantra, beginning with the sound *ṭha*.
One should place the syllable *ha* at the waist, repeating it twelve times;
this is called *hābu* for the two thighs.
Perform the eleventh *hṛdaya* (heart) rotation, naming the two knees with the syllable *ha*.
Perform the second *hṛdaya* rotation, and likewise name the two feet with the Great Space Bindu (*bindu*).
Recite the mantra of the foot-seal (*pādanyāsa*).
This is the method for the secret arrangement of syllables of the Noble Immovable Honored One, the King of Great Wrath,
including nineteen kinds of mantras and their distribution across the various limbs, for the bodhisattva who practices these mantras.
Having performed this arrangement, one’s own body becomes the Holy Lord Sarvadevasūra,
whom neither the bodhisattvas of the ten stages nor any devas or nāgas can ever shake.
Within this assembly of the eight classes of spirits and ghosts,
for the sake of the Sovereign King Īśvara, as well as the Noble Unmoving Honored One, the Great Majestic Wrathful King,
he spoke the mantra of the Great Body, saying:
Namo samantavajrāṇām | amoghehi apratihata-heṭa-ahi-jaḍa-jaṭa-ananta-kān tiṣṭha tiṣṭha jaṇa jaṇa tani ta ||
Ṭa-u-vi-krāntāya maṇirākṣasāya sādhanāya ānaya bandha akṣiṇī kuru asahodana-gṛhṇa gṛhṇa matha matha haṃ haṃ ati.
Mala ehi mahā-yakṣa-viṣana daṭṭha daṭṭha avīśa avīśa a-cala ceṭa sarva-tarānuta-ghātaya ṭaṭa ṭaṭa na-mo na-mo phaṭ phaṭ haṃ ārya.
The Great Majestic Wrathful King Acala further spoke three [mantras].
The samaya-mantra for summoning is as follows:
Namo samantabhadra-pratihatavajrāṇām apratihata-kośānāṃ hūṃ amogha-mahāmaṇi-kośānāṃ hūṃ mahā-tīrtha...
Samayakuru hūṃ trāṭ trāṭ vajralaṭraṭra vajraghaṭa ghaṭa vajranāṭa nāṭa vajrapāṭa he he ḍaṃkuru.
Rusamaya-vajra-mahāmala-vikramaṇānaya-siṃghaṇa-satvabandha-sammarimari-nimuñca muca bandha.
Aṇadamāmani asmin tril-samaya-mahā-māraṅ-kuśi asaha asamaḍni hūṃ hara hara asmin tṛ-hima mahā-māraṅ-kuśi hūṃ akṣaye a.
*Trimālini svāhā.* All [mantras] are identical to those of the Noble Immovable Great Majestic Wrathful King (*Ārya-Acalamahātejorāja*). Furthermore,
he spoke the *samaya-mantra* for protecting the body and binding the boundary (*rakṣā-sīmābandha*), saying:
Namaḥ samantavajrāṇām | Traṭ amoghapāśana mahāraudraṇa sphoṭaya ānaya āśāhe āsamarye hūṃ hūṃ vikiraṇa hūṃ traṭ. O Noble Acala, Greatly Majestic Wrathful King.
Furthermore, the mantra for consecrating one's dwelling place is spoken:
Furthermore, it is said that the incomparable power of the noble Akṣobhya’s mind is the dharma-gate capable of accomplishing all activities.
Perform recitation while subsisting on a vegetarian diet; when the count reaches one hundred thousand repetitions, fast for one day and night.
Only then should you arrange a great offering and perform the homa rite, using wood from the *kṛtavedhana* tree.
Burn two thousand pieces of ghee-soaked [incense], with eight thousand as the limit;
thus the first stage of practice is fulfilled. Whatever one seeks in the heart shall all be accomplished, and whatever words are spoken shall accord with one’s wishes.
Those summoned shall arrive immediately. One who wishes to verify the success of the rite can snap off tree branches, cause birds to fall from flight,
make rivers flow backward, and cause ponds and pools to dry up.
One can cause water to flow upstream, move mountains, and bring about stillness;
one can restrain all non-Buddhist practitioners so that their powers of incantation do not take effect.
Furthermore, regarding the method for accomplishment: wait for the time of a lunar eclipse.
Having fasted for one day and night, one should smear the maṇḍala with the earth from an untrampled area and the dung of a yellow cow; there,
having placed the Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, one should [offer] various exquisite flowers and incense.
Scatter [the substances] upon the altar. One should take ghee from a yellow cow whose calf is of the same color;
take one *liang* of this ghee and place it in a vessel of red copper. Use *khadira* wood [for the ladle].
Churn the clarified butter and perform the consecration; the manifestation of three signs shall occur:
through the sign of warmth, one can achieve the power of subjugation;
through the sign of smoke, one's complexion changes and one's lifespan increases; and the sign of flame appears.
With feet treading upon the void, one attains the state of a Great Sage.
Furthermore, on a mountain peak, by reciting the mantra without food for one hundred thousand repetitions (*lakṣa*), one will be able to see all hidden treasures.
Taking and giving are both mastered; next is the method for removing the calamity of death:
perform *homa* with milk, limited to one thousand repetitions, which can eliminate the misfortunes of death.
Furthermore, this is the method for removing great death.
Using bone-strained *lūka* grass, dip it in ghee, milk, and honey,
and perform *homa* offerings one hundred million times; this can eliminate great calamities of death,
namely those affecting the people of the nation through epidemics and untimely deaths.
Furthermore, regarding the method of accomplishment: by performing *homa* with lotuses dipped in ghee,
curd, honey, and so forth, for one hundred thousand (*lakṣa*) repetitions,
the Great Auspiciousness of the Lotus will be perfected and the celestial maiden will appear before you.
Fulfilling the aspirations of the practitioner:
Next, for the accomplishment of the rite, enter the river flowing into the sea;
standing in it with the water reaching to one's shoulders, perform the recitation for three hundred thousand times.
One obtains a great village; according to the substance used for the homa, one obtains clothing of such a color.
Furthermore, there is a homa method using rice grains:
[one should perform it] with *mṛdvīkā* fruit mixed with honey.
By performing one hundred thousand *homa* offerings, one shall attain the rank of a *rāja*.
Furthermore, regarding the *homa* ritual: by performing one hundred thousand *homa* offerings with *pārijātaka* flowers, one accomplishes the rite of subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*).
Furthermore, by performing homa with pine wood one hundred thousand times,
one will gain the devotion and respect of all people. Furthermore,
by performing homa with barley one hundred thousand times, one will become a great elder.
Next, the ritual rules for painting the image of the Honored One Acala are explained:
one should paint the noble Acala upon a monastic robe (kāṣāya);
his hair hangs down on the right side in a single lock, and his left eye appears squinted.
With his right hand grasping a sharp sword and his left hand holding a noose, he sits serenely upon Mount Ratnaparvata.
Manifesting a roar of defiance and a thunderous cry, he displays a form that strikes terror into the three realms; his entire body is a pervasive azure-blue.

Regarding the aforementioned depiction of the *kāṣāya*: using silk fabrics of vermilion, *kaṇḍa*, or brownish-gray hues and so forth, one creates an image of the *kāṣāya* for the sake of accomplishment;
place it by the shore of a river flowing to the sea.
The practitioner’s robes should be of the prescribed colors;
setting aside all worldly affairs and severing all diverse speech,
one should beg for food and perform recitations until five lakṣas have been completed.
Upon completing the count, one should immediately fast for a full day and night;
one should perform homa with *caṇaka* (chickpeas) mixed with ghee, shaped like *bīja* (beans), with ten thousand as the maximum number.
The Honored One Acala manifests his form; for those who serve and practice, he is like Vagīśvara.
Having attained samādhi, one becomes equal to all the great bodhisattvas and dwells together with them.
Furthermore, regarding the method for painting an image: take the clothing of a deceased person and paint the Noble Acala. His physical appearance is as previously described;
one should draw the eyes of the Acala image using blood drawn from one's own body.
Place the face of the image toward the west; the practitioner of mantras should sit facing the image with their face toward the east.
At all three sessions, one should bathe and wear the wet clothes used for bathing, and maintain silence while performing the recitation.
Recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times; offer various kinds of food and drink to all the spirits and ghosts;
fast for one day and one night on the eighth day of the dark fortnight; and take a corpse that has not yet decayed.
One whose entire body is covered with scars, who possesses all sense faculties in their full integrity,
a youth, a handsome man— when such a corpse is obtained,
one should place it upon the heart and recite the mantra ten thousand times.
The corpse immediately begins to move; the wise one should not fear it.
A wondrous lotus emerges from the corpse’s mouth, which one must then cut off and grasp.
Holding it, one immediately ascends into the air, becoming an accomplished Vidyādhara.
With a physical form like that of Brahmā, one shall become a king among the sages.
If one performs the recitation before an image for three periods each day for a full six months,
making offerings according to one's means and burning aloeswood incense, [the goal will be attained].

One attains the rank of a *jaya* (victory). Furthermore, by performing one thousand additional recitations over a banner and pennant until they are complete, one can subdue enemy armies and quell all adversaries;
[the deity] should be depicted with a large body and yellow color.
The hands on the four sides are likewise four; from the mouth emerge sharp fangs, assuming a form of great ferocity.
His entire body becomes a mass of flames, manifesting the aspect of swallowing the power of others. At all times during battle arrays—
Place the image before the army, as if binding that form with a lasso;
this will cause the enemy to surrender.
If one wishes to accomplish the rite of love, fashion the figure of the person out of salt.
Reciting the name while performing the ritual slicing;
if one performs *homa* within seven days, those of great majesty will all come to submit and follow.
Furthermore, there is another method of accomplishment: if one performs *homa* with *jāti* flowers.
Upon completing one hundred thousand recitations, the medicinal plant *jātī* will come to submit to and follow the vidyādhara. Furthermore,
for the homa rite, one should perform the homa using leaves blown by a whirlwind.
One attains that state of being possessed and driven mad;

furthermore, by performing the rite of *homa* with salt for summoning, one is able to attract all goddesses and summon celestial nymphs (*apsaras*). Moreover, there is the method using *agaru* incense.
By performing the homa rite, one shall become a high minister of the state.
Furthermore, there is another method: paint an image of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and on his right side, paint the form of the youth Mañjuśrī.
On the left, paint Vajrapāṇi in the form of a smiling Bodhisattva;
below him, paint Acala, the Great Fierce Vajra,
adorned with various necklaces and ornaments that embellish his limbs.
Once the painting is finished, recite [the mantra] five hundred thousand times before the image and everything will be accomplished.
To strike down thieves, employ the Eye Seal and recite the HŪṂ mantra; all enemies and adversaries [will be subdued].
One can cause [the target] to fall into madness; the mantra practitioner shall not abandon [the practice] even until [the target’s] death.
Furthermore, to accomplish the rite of subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*), one should burn the ashes of a corpse and empower them seventeen times.
If one scatters [the powder] upon their body, the rite of magnetizing (*vaśīkaraṇa*) will be accomplished.
Furthermore, there is another method: using cow bezoar (*gorocanā*), empower it seven times with mantras and apply a dot between the eyebrows; all beings will then submit.
There shall be no further opposition or rejection. Furthermore,
one visualizes one's own body as taking the form of the Principal Deity,
and arranges the syllables of the mantra upon the various limbs of the body within an area of one hundred yojanas.
It can utterly destroy all those who are difficult to subdue and those possessed by ghosts and spirits;
furthermore, it can extend the life of one whose karmic retribution is exhausted for six months;
and it is like a sword painted upon a wall of Dharma.
With a *kūlika* snake entwined around the sword,
perform one thousand empowerments; visualize the syllable *aḥ* arising within the sword,
emitting blazing light, and have the patient look upon it.
Then, having performed the *avaśeṣa* (concluding rite), the questioner shall speak all things truthfully.
If one recites this one hundred and eight times every day,
the Immovable One (*Acala*) will constantly follow the practitioner of mantras who cultivates the mantra-vidyā.
Whenever there are leftovers from a meal, place them in a clean location and offer them to Acala;
thus one will attain *siddhi* according to one's heart’s desire.
Furthermore, when dividing the wrathful [substances], recite the *HŪṂ* mantra.
It can stop clouds, rain, and the like. Furthermore, there is a method wherein one performs the rite of *homa* using thorny wood;
this can stop great winds and rains and further accomplish all manner of tasks. Next, the method for painting an image:
Upon the *kāṣāya* robe, one should paint hair of blue-black color hanging down toward the left;
he should be depicted in the form of a celibate youth (*kumāra*),
holding a *śakti* in his hand, or grasping a *vajra*.
The eyes are slightly reddish; his majestic radiance is brilliant and blinding.
He sits upon a circular mountain, which is reddish-yellow in color.
He wears garments of blue-green hue and has the appearance of a child.
Regarding this form of the painted image,
one shall achieve the accomplishment of all secret mudrās; whatever matters were previously contemplated,
whether old or new, all shall be fully accomplished.
Regarding all methods for invisibility— whether using wheels, swords, flying through the air, or medicinal herbs—
if these are unavailable, one may simply recite mantras in a secluded place while gazing at this painted image,
and all will be accomplished. Furthermore, there is another method using a mirror.
To examine all matters, whether by consulting a painted image or inquiring about various affairs and so forth, one shall obtain results according to one's wishes.
Furthermore, there is another method: using a healthy boy or girl.
The Ritual for Performing the *Aviśa* [Entrustment]: It is asked: all matters concerning the three periods of time shall be fully accomplished.
Furthermore, the Dharma-gate for the accomplishment of the messenger (*dūta*) is taught: Begin on the first day of the dark fortnight.
Recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times for each of the three periods of the day until the fifteenth day of the waxing moon. When the lunar disk is full,
perform the initial service (*pūrvasevā*) as previously explained.
Using *kaṭuka* wood fuel and white mustard seeds,
begin the *homa* offering at dusk; the messenger will arrive by midnight,
or else remain for the entire night if he does not come.
He will certainly appear; having come to question the vidyādhara, he shall beg for instructions on how to proceed.
One should dispose of him according to one's will, and he shall carry out everything accordingly. If you wish to go to the celestial palace, [he will do so].
The messenger carries them along; he can also bring back the queens,
consorts, and court ladies of Śakra, Lord of Devas,
as well as whatever palaces and pavilions may be required— all of these he is able to procure.
Whether it be tooth-sticks or pure water, or tasks such as anointing and sweeping—
all such duties they can perform; whatever they are commanded to do,
they accomplish it all, just as the Noble One requires.
Cause all these to be accomplished. If the messenger does not appear after one night of *homā*, he shall certainly die;
this is the teaching of the *Ārya-Acala* [Dharmaparyāya]. The exposition of the Dharma gate is now complete.
One fascicle of the Ritual Manual for Recitation of the Most Victorious Standing Mudrā of the Holy Unmoving Wrathful King, from the *Vajrapāṇi-prabhābhiṣeka-tantra*.
